content: I notice that in Mathlib.Algebra.Group.End, right below docs#MulAut.congr, there's some duplicated MulAut and AddAut lemmas. They can't be generated by to_additive as is, since we put a multiplicative structure on both groups. Is there some incantation to fix this?
Oh found it, to_additive_dont_translate
#36156
I need help, I have no idea how to fix the build errors

There's a remark right above docs#Set.conj_mem_fixingSubgroup:

/-
FIXME: The use of `to_additive` in this section is a horrible mess.
It requires translating `MulAut.instGroup` to `AddAut.instAddGroup` instead of `AddAut.instGroup`,
and `MulAut.conj` shouldn't be able to translate to `AddAut.conj`, but somehow it works out.
-/
Maybe the fix here is to translate multiplication on MulAut to addition on AddAut? This would go against mathematical convention I know, but it would make things much easier.
The main issue seems to be docs#MulAut.conj, which we aren't able to translate as docs#AddAut.conj in the current design.

One big issue that I've run into is that we want MulAct G to act on G, and we would like to_additive to translate this into an action of AddAut G on G when G is additive (e.g., these actions for good proofs of lemmas about normal subgroups and normalizers). So whatever translated structure you put on AddAut should also come with a translated action.
But I don't think we have any good additive version of docs#MulDistribMulAction?
i suppose the specific issue with MulAut.conj is that we want MonoidHom to translate to AddChar when the right argument doesn't translate?

Would anything break if we just made the structure on AddAut additive? And if we left some sort of comment "for technical reasons, we break mathematical convention and implement an additive structure instead of a multiplicative one"
Not off the top of my head, although would we need to make a typeclass AddDistribAddAction?

I wrote the quoted comment in a PR not too long ago. My assessment was indeed that MulAut.conj cannot be translated to AddAut.conj. But there are a couple of declarations where this translation IS unexpectedly somehow succeeding. So my suggestion would be to un-to_additivize these declarations. But I couldn't figure out how to do this, because the proof used the group tactic which has no additive counterpart.

This to_additive problem is currently blocking quite a lot of work. If anyone has a better fix, they're welcome to suggest it. Otherwise I'll make a PR to additivize AddAut.

IIUC we want MulAut G to be translated to Additive (AddAut G), and for the Additive part to be canceled where possible.
E.g. def MulAut.conj : G →* MulAut G becomes def AddAut.conj : G →+ Additive (AddAut G),
but instance : Group (MulAut G) becomes instance : AddGroup (Additive (AddAut G)) and then AddGroup+Additive cancel each other to get instance : Group (AddAut G).

Is it possible to add such a feature to to_additive, where we define such cancellative pairs? (another example is Additive G₁ →+ Additive G₂ should cancel to give G₁ →* G₂)
No this is not currently in scope for to_additive.

we want MulAut G to be translated to Additive (AddAut G)

the easiest way to accomplish this is by just making the structure on AddAut G additive :upside_down:
Then it sounds like the best solution, and if and when to_additive supports such a fancy feature we'll "fix" AddAut

Although interestingly, normal_subgroupOf_closure_normalizer uses normalizer_le_normalizer_closure but to_additive works on it. Somehow to_additive picks up on the translated versions, even though they aren't tagged with to_additive existing and have the wrong type.
